nodes.subject: frozen phone and charger matrix
nodes.object: The Realme listing has an anomalous $5.16 no-review display, an included 65 W charger, and a 35-minute seller claim but no named interoperable protocol. UGREEN is a $22.99, 17-review, one-port 65 W PD route with a 100 W-capable cable. Cirtek is a $49.99 no-review multiport route whose 100 W headline falls to stated per-port allocations under simultaneous use. None supplies an independent Realme safety or aging test.

nodes.subject: delivered phone charging power
nodes.object: The actual rate is bounded by the device, negotiated protocol, charger port, cable, and simultaneous allocation. USB-C shape is not a protocol, Quick Charge requires both endpoints, a 100 W cable does not raise a 65 W brick above 65 W, and neither third-party listing establishes the unnamed Realme Smart Flash profile.

nodes.subject: fast-charge safety and longevity evidence
nodes.object: Seller protection, GaN, speed, and battery-life language is not longitudinal evidence. Generic cell, charger, and BMS mechanisms identify material, heat, voltage, current, and control variables but do not measure the Realme. Conflicting anonymous owner reports cannot prove that 65 W necessarily helps or harms this battery.

nodes.subject: one-brick charging preflight
nodes.object: Verify Realme protocol and profiles, laptop input, port allocation, cable requirement, and reconnect behavior, then run bounded single-device and simultaneous screen-off trials that record charge interval, interruptions, negotiated indication, and device temperature warnings. Different-model anecdotes do not substitute for this test.
